words.definition: A word you say when you meet someone or answer the phone.
words.example: Hello! Is this Maria's phone?

words.definition: A word you say when you leave someone or end a call.
words.example: Goodbye! See you next week.

words.definition: A polite word you add when you ask for something.
words.example: Could you open the window, please?

words.definition: A short, casual way to say you are grateful.
words.example: Thanks for the ride. I really appreciate it.

words.definition: Feeling bad about something you did or something that happened.
words.example: I'm sorry I'm late. The bus was slow.

words.definition: A friendly word you say when someone arrives.
words.example: Welcome to our home! Come on in.

words.definition: To forgive a small mistake. "Excuse me" is also a polite way to get someone's attention.
words.example: Excuse me, is this seat taken?

words.definition: To see and talk to someone, for the first time or by plan.
words.example: Nice to meet you! I'm Daniel.

words.definition: The word people use to call a person or thing.
words.example: What's your name? Sorry, I didn't catch it.

words.definition: A person you know well and like.
words.example: My best friend lives next door.

words.definition: Your female parent.
words.example: My mother makes the best soup.

words.definition: Your male parent.
words.example: My father drives a taxi in the city.

words.definition: A girl or woman who has the same parents as you.
words.example: Do you have a sister or a brother?

words.definition: A boy or man who has the same parents as you.
words.example: My little brother never cleans his room.

words.definition: A mother or a father.
words.example: One parent has to sign this form.

words.definition: The mother of your mother or father.
words.example: We visit my grandmother every summer.

words.definition: The man a woman is married to.
words.example: Her husband works at a hospital.

words.definition: The woman a man is married to.
words.example: He called his wife to say he'd be late.

words.definition: A very young child.
words.example: The baby finally fell asleep!

words.definition: A group of people who are related, like parents and children.
words.example: Our family eats dinner together every night.

words.definition: The number 1.
words.example: I have one brother.

words.definition: The number 2.
words.example: We have two cats.

words.definition: The number 3.
words.example: Take three tablets a day.

words.definition: The number 4.
words.example: There are four seats.

words.definition: The number 5.
words.example: It's five minutes away.

words.definition: The number 6.
words.example: I wake up at six.

words.definition: The number 7.
words.example: There are seven days in a week.

words.definition: The number 8.
words.example: The class starts at eight.

words.definition: The number 9.
words.example: He's nine years old.

words.definition: The number 10.
words.example: I'll be there in ten minutes.

words.definition: To stop sleeping. People often say "wake up".
words.example: What time do you wake up on weekdays?

words.definition: Washing your body under falling water.
words.example: I take a shower before breakfast.

words.definition: To clean or smooth something with a brush.
words.example: Don't forget to brush your teeth!

words.definition: The first meal of the day.
words.example: We had eggs and toast for breakfast.

words.definition: A hot brown drink that helps many people wake up.
words.example: Would you like some coffee?

words.definition: A loud sound that wakes you up or warns you of danger.
words.example: My alarm didn't go off this morning.

words.definition: To put clothes on. People often say "get dressed".
words.example: Get dressed. We leave in ten minutes!

words.definition: A soft bag you put your head on in bed.
words.example: I need a softer pillow.

words.definition: A piece of cloth you use to dry yourself.
words.example: Can you hand me that towel?

words.definition: To move or act fast because you do not have much time.
words.example: Hurry up, or we'll miss the bus!

words.definition: The room where you cook food.
words.example: She's cooking in the kitchen.

words.definition: The room where you sleep.
words.example: My bedroom gets a lot of sun.

words.definition: The room with a toilet and usually a sink and shower.
words.example: Where's the bathroom, please?

words.definition: The part you open to go in or out of a room or building.
words.example: Please close the door behind you.

words.definition: An opening in a wall with glass, so you can see outside.
words.example: It's hot in here. Can we open a window?

words.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat top, used for eating or working.
words.example: Dinner is on the table!

words.definition: A seat for one person, usually with a back.
words.example: Pull up a chair and sit with us.

words.definition: The surface you walk on inside a room.
words.example: Careful, the floor is wet.

words.definition: A set of steps that take you up or down inside a building.
words.example: Our apartment is up two flights of stairs.

words.definition: A small metal object you use to open a lock.
words.example: I can't find my keys anywhere.

words.definition: A common food made from flour and baked.
words.example: Can you buy some bread on your way home?

words.definition: Small white or brown grains that you cook and eat.
words.example: Do you want rice or noodles with that?

words.definition: An oval food from a hen that you can boil, fry or scramble.
words.example: How do you like your eggs?

words.definition: A white drink that comes from cows.
words.example: We're out of milk.

words.definition: A solid food made from milk.
words.example: Could I get extra cheese on my pizza?

words.definition: A round fruit that is red, green or yellow.
words.example: I packed an apple for lunch.

words.definition: A bird kept for food, or its meat.
words.example: I'm going to order the grilled chicken.

words.definition: The clear liquid you drink.
words.example: Could I have a glass of water?

words.definition: A hot liquid food, often with vegetables or meat.
words.example: This soup is too hot to eat yet.

words.definition: A sweet white or brown substance used in food and drinks.
words.example: No sugar in my tea, thanks.

words.definition: On this day.
words.example: What are you doing today?

words.definition: On the day after today.
words.example: I have a dentist appointment tomorrow.

words.definition: On the day before today.
words.example: I forgot to call you yesterday.

words.definition: The early part of the day, before noon.
words.example: I go running every morning.

words.definition: The part of the day between afternoon and night.
words.example: Are you free this evening?

words.definition: The dark part of the day, when most people sleep.
words.example: I couldn't sleep last night.

words.definition: A period of seven days.
words.example: I work four days a week.

words.definition: A period of sixty seconds.
words.example: Wait a minute, I'll be right back.

words.definition: Saturday and Sunday.
words.example: Any plans for the weekend?

words.definition: After the expected or correct time.
words.example: Sorry, I'm running late.

words.definition: Used before a singular noun when you mean one.
words.example: I need a pen.

words.definition: Used before a vowel sound instead of "a".
words.example: She eats an apple every day.

words.definition: Used when the person or thing is known.
words.example: Close the door, please.

words.definition: A word that joins two things.
words.example: I like tea and coffee.

words.definition: A word that means "while", "because" or "in the way that".
words.example: She sang as she worked.

words.definition: A word that makes a sentence negative.
words.example: I'm not hungry.

words.definition: A word that shows a part of something or belonging.
words.example: A cup of tea, please.

words.definition: A word that shows direction or purpose.
words.example: I'm going to the shop.

words.definition: A word that shows purpose or who gets something.
words.example: This gift is for you.

words.definition: To exist, or to have a particular quality.
words.example: I want to be a doctor.

words.definition: To own, or to eat or drink.
words.example: I have two brothers.

words.definition: To the inside of something.
words.example: She walked into the room.

words.definition: Away from or no longer on something.
words.example: Turn off the light.

words.definition: Away from the inside.
words.example: Let's go out for dinner.

words.definition: To a higher position.
words.example: Stand up, please.

words.definition: To a lower position.
words.example: Sit down, please.

words.definition: A word used after a negative to add another negative.
words.example: I don't like tea, nor do I like coffee.

words.definition: A formal word for "who" as the object of a verb.
words.example: To whom should I send this?

words.definition: Used to ask who something belongs to.
words.example: Whose bag is this?

words.definition: In or to any place.
words.example: Sit wherever you like.

words.definition: Having the color of blood or a ripe tomato.
words.example: Stop when the light is red.

words.definition: Having the color of a clear sky.
words.example: The sky is so blue today!

words.definition: Having the color of grass.
words.example: I'd like the green one, please.

words.definition: Having the color of a lemon or the sun.
words.example: She painted her kitchen yellow.

words.definition: Having the darkest color, like night.
words.example: He always drinks his coffee black.

words.definition: Having the color of milk or snow.
words.example: We need white paint for the walls.

words.definition: Having the color of chocolate or earth.
words.example: She has long brown hair.

words.definition: Having a light red color.
words.example: The sunset turned the sky pink.

words.definition: Having a color between red and blue.
words.example: Do you have this shirt in purple?

words.definition: Having a color between black and white.
words.example: It's a gray, rainy morning.
